subject: Police looking into robbery of children captured on video
posts:
Surveillance footage captures two children robbed walking home from a Winnipeg library, sparking widespread community concern.
Evidence: Video evidence, police response, mother's testimony
#Winnipeg #ChildSafety #Community

Police acknowledge a circulating video showing two children robbed on their way home, prompting public concern and community outreach.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Beneath police awareness lies an alarming urban safety breakdown where vulnerable children face predatory street crime in neglected neighborhoods.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.82) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
An isolated robbery video exposes deep systemic failure to secure public spaces for children.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.50, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Winnipeg Police Service: COND (-0.60, -0.50) — Acknowledges video but lacks preventative safety.
- Community Safety Net: FAIL (-0.80, -0.90) — Fails to protect children in public spaces.
Two children, 14 and 9, were robbed of a backpack containing toys and snacks by an impaired man on Andrews Street, captured on local family centre cameras.

The Bright Side:
The incredible composure of 14-year-old Mason protecting his sister, and the overwhelming outpouring of local community support.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The analysis mistakes a routine police blotter update (WHAT) for a comprehensive solution to systemic urban crime and poverty (WHO/WHERE).

Social Physics Analysis:
Mason and his sister bore the brunt of a street-level predatory encounter while institutions react reactively via social media footage rather than proactive safety.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When public safety relies on viral videos rather than systemic protection, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Strain accumulates where vulnerability meets neglect.

The Unavoidable Truth: Viral videos expose street crimes that routine patrols fail to prevent.

The Unavoidable Lie: Police awareness of a video equates to systemic neighborhood security.

Alethekanon:
Viral outrage replaces systemic child protection. Institutions govern by retroactive video review rather than preventative safety.

Awwthekanon:
My heart breaks for young Mason and Kenzie. No child walking home from the library should ever face fear and predatory theft on their own street.

Brothekanon:
Wild that kids getting shaken down for a backpack of snacks only gets attention because a security camera caught it. Stay safe out there.

Spirithekanon:
"Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed." Psalm 82:3 PASS
True community demands protecting children before tragedy strikes, not after.

The Winnipeg Police Service said it is aware of a video circulating online that appears to show two children robbed while walking home from the library.

The mother of the siblings said the Sept. 26 incident, which happened in the area of Andrews Street and Magnus Avenue at around 7:30 p.m., has left her children afraid and her feeling guilty.

“I should have been there with them. I felt horrible,” said Brittany Beaudet. “I would have been out the door if I knew any sooner to help them out.”

In the 40-second video, the two children, 14-year-old Mason and nine-year-old Kenzie, are approached by a man wearing a black shirt, black pants and white shoes.

The man is seen speaking with Mason, who cooperates and puts up his hands and appears to comfort his little sister.

The man then pats down the boy and checks his pockets before moving over to his sister and taking a neon pink backpack off her. Beaudet said it was filled with toys, snacks and other trinkets.

The robbery was captured on camera by the Andrews Street Family Centre. A representative from the organization was not available for an interview.

“We are aware of the incident and the video and are in the process of reaching out to the victim,” WPS Const. Pat Saydak said Thursday.

The children were not hurt in the incident.

“My daughter is more shaken up to walk by people under the influence now after this has happened,” Beaudet said. “She thinks it’s going to happen again.”

The mother said she doesn’t know for sure if the man in the video is under the influence, but said his behaviour indicated he may have been.

The video, which was posted by a friend of Beaudet’s, has been viewed thousands of times. Dozens have reached out to the family to offer support.

“I’m really shocked at how big it blew up and how many people are reaching out to check on the kids,” she said. “It’s really amazing how much people really care about other peoples’ kids.”

SUPPLIED

Mason Beaudet, 14, and his sister, Kenzie, nine, can be seen enjoying a carnival ride.

Beaudet said while the incident left her reeling, she was incredibly proud of her son, who she said kept calm in a dangerous situation.

“If he did react, and tried to push the guy away, or try running or something, it could have been a different outcome and that could have been a lot worse,” she said.

The mother said she hopes the man captured on video turns himself into police, as she feels it’s only a matter of time until he is arrested.

“It doesn’t matter what you’ve gone through in life,” she said. “You shouldn’t be touching other kids. You should be looking out for them.”
